Deleted an article by Edmund pao at -25 with three staff votes, standard deletion process.

Description : Scp 5136 is a dream that will go from victim to victim. Although the dream can take many forms, the most common form taken is a child like face with hollow eyes spiked hair and a dirty face. Scp 5136 'S hunting pattern is unknown, and can take place anywhere on earth so long the person is alive.

No feedback present.

Deleted an article by KelvinKW at -19 with three staff votes, standard deletion process.

Description: SCP-5968 is a gaming headphone that is capable of terminating any of its users. SCP-5968 is covered in a layer of rust and is made of a highly toxic metal that resembles chlorine. Although it does not react violently towards air, it will decay any metal and cells that it touches. SCP-5968 is capable of moving after the subject puts on the set. It is not yet able to sustain complete control of the subject since it decays the subject in such a violent way that the subject will die in approximately 2 minutes.

No feedback present.

Deleted an article by Coleton richardson at -18 with three staff votes, standard deletion process.

Description: SCP-5161 is a wooden children’s toy more commonly known as “Cup-And-Ball” with a red circle on the top end of the “cup” with green and black lines of the outer end of the “cup.”

Feedback is as follows:

+ ISNorden
– ISNorden

Having an anomalous low-tech game with built-in auto-cheating? Makes sense.

Using the player's muscle mass to repair damage to itself? Makes less sense for a game that depends mainly on hand-eye coordination; I'd have this skip inflict similar neurological damage, worsening vision and motor/manual skills instead of taking a literal pound of flesh.

Deleted an article by Reonicles19 at -17 with three staff votes, standard deletion process.

Description: SCP - 5179 is a winged serpent with no head or tail, rather the entity is a self enclosed loop and is often twisted so it can compress itself when in smaller areas. The entity has many sets of white feathered wings along its body at regular intervals. On the body segment of the entity, between the set of wings is a large eye with a diameter of 65 centimeters. The eyes are of different animals at different points in the entity’s body. The eyes of horses, cats, dogs, fish, humans, snakes and their close relatives have been noted on the entity's body but larger than their natural sizes. SCP - 5179 is covered in pale gold fur which has a lustrous quality to it.

+ Daemon2266
– Daemon2266

Good idea, but it needs to be written differently. For instance, "SCP - 5179 is to be contained in a container which is made of bismuth metal sheeting on all surfaces." Change repetitive statements like 'contained in a container' and find new, less redundant ways of expressing your ideas. Check out some of the other SCPs and check out how the authors wrote their articles. It might be a good idea to take notes on how they write their articles to see how you can redo this article for the better.

Deleted an article by DrPepperThePeeper at -13 with three staff votes, standard deletion process.

Description: SCP-5171 appears as a tunnel with a road running through it located under a bridge. The tunnel itself is a gateway to an area in between space and time, which is classified as SCP-5171-1. SCP-5171-1 appears to be infinite grasslands with a dirt road running through them. The weather inside SCP-5171-1 has been observed to always be raining, however the substance raining from the sky is not considered to be water. The substance raining from the sky inside of SCP-5171-1 appears to be a mixture of tears and blood. The origin of these substances is still unknown, as the clouds inside SCP-5171-1 are non-anomalous.

No feedback present.

Deleted an article by KSforShort at -11 with three staff votes, standard deletion process.

Description: SCP-5129 is a frog carved out of jade, measuring 10 centimeters in length and dated to be approximately 1000 years old. When in its inactive state, it displays no anomalous characteristics. Once activated by its intended user (SCP-5129-1), it begins to emit harmless levels of █████████ radiation, and air pressure within a 3 meter sphere drops to 27.50 Hg. SCP-5129-1 then telepathically hears a voice1 which is unanimously described as having a deep, booming quality. In every test to date, this voice has only been reported saying: "DO YOU WISH TO EMERGE?" If SCP-5129-1 declines, then SCP-5129 immediately returns to an inactive state.

Feedback is as follows:

+ Zyn
– Zyn

Proper clinical tone for an SCP write-up

I'm personally going to disagree with this—there are several instances of non-clinical phrasing, immediately from the description:

SCP-5129 is a small frog carved out of jade, dated to be approximately one thousand years old. While inactive, it displays no anomalous characteristics. When activated by its intended user (who shall be referred to as SCP-5129-1), it begins to emit harmless levels of █████████ radiation, and air pressure within a ten foot sphere drops to 27.50 Hg.

  • "Small" is a vague measurement and can vary in visualization between individuals. Better to give an objective measurement of the frog so people can immediately know what size it is beyond "small".
  • Numbers greater than 10 (and all measurements with units) should be written as numbers, not words. "Approximately 1000 years".
  • The second sentence can be removed since it's kind of commonsense?
  • The bit in the parentheses is overly long, and can be shortened to "designated SCP-5129-1".
  • Feet are not metric measurements; meters should be used instead.
  • It's not stated where the spherical effect occurs with relation to the object.

The rest of the article has similarly non-clinical writing. Not a huge deal all things considered, but noticeable enough to break immersion for some readers.

Footnotes
1. This voice always speaks in the first or preferred language of SCP-5129-1

SCP-5978 is a hourglass, standing 9.5 inches tall and has a 6-inch base. Around the glass, consists of golden swirly bars that protect the hourglass from breaking.

Deleted at -19 and three votes.

SCP-5127 apparents to be a regular fridge, from both the inside and outside, it measures 60 inches in height and 28 in depth. Everytime someone opens its door any drink or food randomly appears, it looks like it can also randomly bring objects to it's inside. SCP-5127 can only grab any food or drink if it is within a 5 miles range, otherwise when you open it, it will absorb any organic material within 5 milles range, including water from a human body or even flesh. SCP-5127 apparents to have incurable effects on those who had their flesh ripped off.

Deleted at -15 and three votes.

SCP-5159 is an elderly male of American descent, measuring 1.6 meters in height, and 72 kilograms in weight. SCP-5159 speaks with a southern American accent, has blue eyes, and gray hair, though he is practically bald. SCP-5159 is roughly 80-90 years of age and has not aged since its discovery by the foundation. A tattoo reading “Mr. Emotions, from Little Misters ® by Dr. Wondertainment" appears on the back of SCP-5159’s neck.

Deletion at -15 and three votes.

Feedback Ported:

eric_h

+ show block
– hide block

I'll throw a few comments in before this goes away…

— A couple very basic pet peeves:

No SCP should be allowed to wander around the containment site.

When something "appears" to do or be something, the implication is it is/does something completely different and the actual thing should be interesting enough to elaborate on somewhere in the article.

— The "Dr. Wondertainment" aspect doesn't really suit this object and feels tacked on.

— This guy is pretty much a living Mood Ring, which is somewhat amusing but you need to take that somewhere interesting. Since it's a pretty straightforward anomalous effect, maybe the way to go is to give him a good backstory. I was hoping to see that in the interview, but it didn't really add anything. There wasn't a hook on this one to make it at all memorable.

item.content:encoded:
SCP-5217 Was found back in 2003 after a civilian came into contact with a seemingly normal gelatine product, or jelly bean, and fell into a deep coma dying only hours later police officers were called to analyse the product and found a elemental composition that is unfound in normal versions of this product. Later analysis shows that this product has a living biological composition and naturally releases a toxic gas into the air nearby and is coated in a poison similar to that of a poison dart frog

Deleted at -19 and three votes.

SCP-5368, otherwise known as The Gun, The gun is a Mauser M1887 the gun was made for ww1, country of origin Germany we believe it was made by Königliche Waffen Schmieden in 1918 but we have no proof of this.

Deleted at -17 and three votes.

A Second Chance

“Doctor Vasily Borodin is hereby found guilty of crimes against humanity, and is therefore sentenced to hang until death.”

The courtroom erupts into applause after the verdict is stated.
Vasily is quiet. He feels the weight of death over life looming over him, but most of all intense hatred for these fools who’s minds were clouded by ignorance.

Deleted at -14 and three votes.

SCP-5279-1 is a small seemingly indestructible cardboard box that houses SCP-5279-2, testing shows it’s resistant to fire, gunfire, blunt force, high caliber explosions, and even being doused in lava. Besides SCP-5279-1’s inability to be destroyed or even damaged, the box appears to have no other unusual effects and simply acts as a casing for SCP-5279-2.

Deleted at -13 and three votes.

Feedback Ported:

Doggol

+ show block
– hide block

This needs expansion. Why is it a coca-cola brand ball? Why does it kill you? It just doesn't really work, in my opinion.

A few things:

testing shows it’s resistant to fire, gunfire, blunt force, high calibre explosions, and even being doused in lava

Why would they test these things? When they discovered it, they would have realised it was indestructible, and it seems like it would be a waste of resources to just hit it with everything they have to destroy it. Just because something is indestructible doesnt mean that that fact needs to be tested, especially as foundation policy is to keep anomalies around.

it will start flashing the colors of the rainbow once something black, green, or shiny enters 2 feet within the radius of SCP-5279-2 or SCP-5279-1

If it goes within 2 feet1 of itself, it activates? Because it is SCP-5279-2.

In general, this article has no narrative, and even an anomaly that's interesting on its own doesnt really work without that. So … -1.

SCP-3873 is a female human named Riley ██████, birth date ██/██/9█. The subject is Caucasian in descent, possessing primarily Aryan features. SCP-3873 was born in ████, Florida. The biological parents of SCP-3873 went missing in 20██ due to SCP-3873-1 events.

Deleted at -11 and three votes.

Feedback Ported:

RJB_R

+ show block
– hide block

I really, really enjoyed this. The weird details like the anomaly not affecting people with severed digits was a good start, I honestly enjoyed the description alone enough to upvote this. While I liked the first interview, I was afraid there was going to become a case of too much extra content bringing down the concise and solid main description, but then the escalation of the effect and the story that was told sucked me in.

I love that it gives enough description of the cult to keep us interested without giving everything away. My only quibble is that I feel the Foundation using D-Class from the area where SCP-3873 came from seems like a serious oversight, but you could fix that by making it so the D-Class was recruited from somewhere else in the USA, maybe with a name change, and it wasn't initially apparent he came from Florida. Also, there's a broken collapsible in the addendum area.

Easy upvote and I really hope this gets the attention it deserves because it is a masterwork of an SCP.

(account deleted)

+ show block
– hide block

I strongly dislike this.

The subject is Caucasian in descent, possessing blonde hair, blue eyes, and pale skin.

You call the skip the subject and not the anomaly or the object. (I'm seeing that error more and more these days — did we stop trying to enforce that or something?) And I keep trying to figure out why it's so hard to refrain from saying "why did you describe an Aryan" — it's not like people aren't allowed to look like that, lol — so I think it's because "pale skin" is wholly unnecessary when you already specify race.

The whole thing about letting a D-class stay with her was terrifying. I like writing the Foundation as 'the nice side of cold' too but this is too far IMO; the dude's a violent felon. What the hell is the Ethics Committee on in this? The Foundation's job isn't to make sure she's got someone to cuddle with, it's to stop her from hurting people/disrupting normality and keep her safe from herself in the process.

And he ended up hurting her, which just makes their move look dumber from a narrative standpoint regardless of the fact that he did it because he was in the cult. Like, the fact that chances led to him being from the cult just proves that they shouldn't have done it. It's not a good way to introduce the notion of letting someone stay with a skip.

Before security could intervene, Junior Researcher Davis had entered the cell and engaged D-36336 in an attempt to divert his attention from SCP-3873. Agent White discharged his firearm at D-36336, grazing JR Davis's left arm, penetrating D-36336's collarbone, and exiting through the shoulderblade. At which point, D-36336 desisted before being approached, shot again, and killed by Agent White. SCP-3873 was examined by medical staff and treated for minor blunt force trauma.

So was Agent White reprimanded for killing a subject who surrendered? Why was he using lethal force in a containment chamber with only one normal human perpetrator anyway? Even civilian tasers can have a range of 25 feet and this room cannot possibly be that big. The Foundation values lives. Even D-class ones, because they need living human bodies to use. Killing someone like this is a waste of personnel. If his behavior is too shit for anything else, he can be amnesticized and assigned to something that doesn't require interacting with a sapient entity.

SCP-3873: That's it, huh? Just a report? Paperwork? I am a person, doctor! I am a human, just like you!

Dr. Porter pauses.

Dr. Porter: I know, Riley. We all know. There are many more like you. Many more who continue to suffer fates that we wish we could help them out of. But we can't. That's a reality that most of us have come to accept. The multiverse is a cruel place. I'm sorry. We have to get back to work now.

The 'I'm sapient waah'/'we don't care I'm doing my job' skip/employee exchange trope is not unique in general or in this application.

It was concluded that the effect had somehow passed onto him when it was neutralized from the initial SCP-3873 host.

Nothing has been established to indicate that this is a thing that can happen. Dropping it as a surprise at the end just leaves more unanswered questions, and not in a good way.

It has been determined that Dr. Porter contracted the anomaly by sheer chance.

Yeah.

Locating the current host of the anomaly is a Delta-level priority. I have assigned Mobile Task Force Iota-10 to monitor governmental and judicial chatter to locate the current host and place them into containment. We have a whole world to search. We will not make this mistake again.

That's cool, but no focus is put on these elements at all until here. The story is about a girl being miserable while men make her miserable, and then the narrative tries to switch to the wide-scale look at the cult's impact on the world instead. The end result is split focus.

Between these nitpicks and some social issue elements I'll refrain from addressing in depth because they're subjective, this whole thing is just uncomfortable and clashes with my headcanon egregiously.

Rioghail

+ show block
– hide block

The biggest problem for me is how contrived it is. There's a bunch of really contrived plotting here (the Foundation being willing to leave 3873 and the D-Class together unsupervised for such a long time, the D-Class being a member of the cult, Porter getting the effect by chance), so much so that I initially thought this was one of those articles where someone in the Foundation is removing information to hide something. If that was the intent, and the researchers are covering something up, then it doesn't really coalesce well enough and seems unmotivated. If that wasn't the intent, then this plotting is just extremely contrived and unbelievable.

Drblackbox

+ show block
– hide block

Mirroring this, Once a character makes so many blatantly bad and irrational choices like the foundation does here it is hard to take it seriously. Really it seems that they lucked out that it didn't go even more wrong and kill some random civilians or something. Or that the D-class was a cultist and didn't kill her or something, I know we should humanize villains and not make them pure evil but generally being in prison doesn't mean you can be trusted to your own devices ever again. There's a reason homicide almost always means no chance of being in public again.

Footnotes
1. By the way, that needs to be in metric, as the foundation uses UN standard units

item.title: SCP Announcements 47: Life is like riding a bicycle.: Re: SCP Announcements 47: Life is like riding a bicycle.
item.content:encoded:
As a general note, feedback should ideally be sought before a mainlist post. Readers who vote on articles are not obligated to explain their vote; furthermore, if a piece is negatively rated, reviewers may not be keen to post critique if the page and its discussion thread will be deleted.

The How to Write an SCP Guide has instructions on where/how to seek feedback before posting material to the mainlist.
